findings.title: Signs passed, allegiance divided
findings.claim: The signs occupy the whole heaven-and-earth field, yet the people pass over them while turning away; 12:106 places belief beside association, allowing aversion to be read within a believing but divided orientation, as refusal of the sign's exclusive claim rather than proof of total nonrecognition.
findings.mechanism: The focus makes the sign the object of passage and withdrawal. 12:106 holds belief in God and association together in one clause, so the nearby turning-away can be read as refusal of the sign's exclusive claim within a believing stance, not as proof of total ignorance. The trusted channel names partial belief and divided allegiance; the HFT participation trace remains attributed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see that bodily proximity to signs, and even belief, do not by themselves amount to undivided recognition.
findings.containment: The adjacency invites the comparison but does not prove that every passer is among the people described as believing and associating in 12:106. The sky and earth branches retain their ordinary domain meanings; no cloud, covering, or other homonymous branch is implied.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence and exact focus/context wording support the core relation; one represented HFT branch has legacy_unbound provenance and remains attributed, and the link between the two populations is not asserted as identity.

findings.title: A story's lesson must cross over
findings.claim: The focus can describe movement that remains interpretively incomplete until a story's events cross into admonition for the reader: 12:111 names the stories, a lesson, detail, and guidance.
findings.mechanism: The focus sign is passed while people turn away. In 12:111, following a story's sequence leads to ʿibrah, a lesson taken from one condition for another, then detail and guidance. These contextual operations change the focus failure from mere lack of pause into a possible failure to carry an observed case into one's own way.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how a narrative trace becomes useful when its outcome travels into present judgment.
findings.containment: This is an attributed analogy between passing and the lesson/crossing sequence. The word ʿibrah may carry its lesson sense without activating a spatial crossing in the earlier verb.

epistemic.reason: The exact context roots and indices agree with the packet; the movement from narrative lesson to the focus passing remains a qualified HFT inference.

findings.title: The sign-field is also named as creation
findings.claim: The same heaven-and-earth pair that hosts the focus signs has already appeared in Yusuf's prayer as what God originated; he also addresses God as his protector, placing the focus's sign-field within an explicitly created and guarded cosmos.
findings.mechanism: 12:101 repeats the exact paired domain and predicates God as its originator and the speaker's protector. That independent contextual relation changes the heavens and earth from scenery alone into a world Yusuf acknowledges as made and held, against the focus's report of people turning from its signs.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice that this story has already voiced recognition of the very domains in which the focus locates overlooked signs.
findings.containment: This is a pericope juxtaposition, not a claim that the passers heard Yusuf's prayer or that 12:105 explicitly defines each sign as a proof of creation.

epistemic.reason: The exact paired nouns and creator/protector wording are supplied, but connecting Yusuf's prayer to the focus is an authored contextual inference with no dedicated support record.

findings.title: From reminder to sign-field
findings.claim: Immediately before the focus places signs in the heavens and earth, the pericope calls its preceding message a reminder for the worlds; the sequence sets a conveyed reminder beside signs encountered throughout the cosmos.
findings.mechanism: 12:104 names a reminder addressed to the worlds, and 12:105 moves directly to abundant signs in the heavens and earth that people pass. This adjacency changes the scale of attention from a communicated reminder to the environment through which people move.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the focus as a move from hearing a reminder to encountering signs across the world around them.
findings.containment: The adjacent verses do not identify every cosmic sign with the preceding message; the relation is sequential and complementary, not an equation.

epistemic.reason: Both ayat and their order are supplied directly; the complementary relation between spoken reminder and cosmic signs is an authored inference.

findings.title: A communal answer to turning away
findings.claim: The added 1:5 gives the focus a concrete first-person-plural counter-response: worship and asking help are directed to one addressee, in tension with the adjacent statement of belief alongside association.
findings.mechanism: The focus participle names withdrawal from signs, 12:106 states belief with association, and 1:5 repeats the fronted 'You alone' before both 'we worship' and 'we seek help'. This adds an affirmative communal form of devotion and dependence beyond the host passage's path-and-insight wording.
findings.reader_payoff: The overlay makes a response to the sign-field speakable as shared devotion and dependence, not only as a route of guided attention.
findings.containment: This is an overlay contrast, not a lexical definition of turning away or proof that the Fatiha's worshippers and the focus passers are the same people. The host passage already supplies its own path and warning.

epistemic.reason: The native belief/association contact is supported by trusted channel evidence, while the extension to the individually supplied 1:5 prayer is a bounded overlay inference.
